text:
Anna K: Ran an nsys trace on the latest runtime build (kv-prefetch + continuous-batching) — timeline looks noisy: lots of tiny cudaMemcpy + kernel selector CPU work between kernels. uploaded: https://perf.internal/trace/1842109876 :eyes:
perf-bot: nsys trace uploaded: https://perf.internal/trace/1842109876 (profile id 2026-03-gpu-run)
Mike L: Can you paste a short timeline screenshot? also curious: are you using NVTX ranges around selector calls or only around kernel launches?
Anna K: Screenshot: (attached). We currently NVTX around: request-level, token-gen, and each kernel launch (name = kernel_name). Selector is not NVTX'd, just visible as CPU stacks.
Sara P: Two quick thoughts: 1) add a thin NVTX span for selector decisions so we can correlate which selector path led to which kernel timeline. 2) avoid extremely long span names — they explode nsys loading time.
Raj D: For (1) +1. Ideally span names should be compact but parseable. I propose a small convention: "R:<reqid>|M:<model_tag>|B:<batch>|S:<seq_len>|K:<choice_code>". Example: "R:9a7f|M:gpt8s|B:4|S:128|K:Q2". Keep under ~64 chars.
Mike L: Love compact encoding. Also think we need two levels: (a) per-request 'request' span that is human-readable ("req 9a7f model gpt8s b4") and (b) per-op compact tags for perf tooling. We can synthesize the readable name in post-processing from compact tags.
Anna K: Agree. One pain point: adding NVTX for every tiny op increases trace overhead and changes timing (sampling shows ~5-8% overhead with current NVTX pattern). Maybe we should sample selector spans (1 in N) or only enable verbose NVTX in debug profiles.
Sara P: We saw that too. Another option: use a single NVTX range for "selector-phase" that encapsulates multiple selector ops but push metadata as payloads or colors. nvtxRangePushEx allows numeric payload -> cheap to parse later.
Raj D: For caching, we should tag selector hits vs misses. Selector misses followed by kernel fallback are the hard cases. Proposed tags: K:HIT, K:MISS and a small numeric code for fallback reason. Add it to the per-request compact tag so in perf you can filter for MISS cases quickly.
Mike L: Also noticed kernel-launch backlog is often because of small batch kernel choices — the kernel selector sometimes picks full attention kernel for seq<max due to conservative thresholds. We should log selector heuristic decisions as metrics (counter) and key them by (model_arch, quant, batch_range, seq_range). Make those visible in traces as counters if possible.
Anna K: Re: nvprof vs perfetto: perfetto native traces show better interleaving for CPU<->GPU; nsys is still better for per-kernel timelines. I ran both and linked both traces in the upload. We should standardize the job name and include git sha + config flags in NVTX top-level span to cross-ref traces.
Sara P: Sample push/pop snippet I use:
```
// C++
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.colorType = NVTX_COLOR_ARGB;
attr.color = 0xFF3377CC;
attr.messageType = NVTX_MESSAGE_TYPE_ASCII;
attr.message.ascii = short_name; // compact tag
nvtxRangePushEx(&attr);
// ... work ...
nvtxRangePop();
```
Use short_name = "R:9a7f|M:g8s|B:04|K:Q2" and separately emit a JSON line to logs mapping compact->human.
Raj D: Good. One more micro-optimization: use nvtxNameCudaStream() or attach ranges to streams rather than pushing/popping around every tiny memcpy. That avoids frequent host-side ops.
Mike L: Regarding KV cache behavior: traces show high variance when cache prefetch misses. We should instrument "kvcache:lookup" and "kvcache:prefetch" with a small integer payload (hit=1/miss=0/prefetch=2) so perf scripts can color by value.
Anna K: I'll add payload-based ranges for kvcache and selector. Will also add explicit span for "kernel-selection-cache-lookup" that runs in the selector thread. If we still see high overhead, we flip to sampled NVTX (1/10 traces) and rely on logs + metrics for the rest.
Sara P: Also add request_id -> nvtx payload pointer (64-bit) linking to an in-memory sample struct. Perf scripts can read that pointer if necessary to join trace->logs in post.
Mike L: Action items:
- Anna: land compact NVTX naming + payloads for selector + kvcache (PR please including example trace link) -> due EOD tomorrow
- Raj: add selector fallback counters + expose as metrics in /metrics
- Sara: update perf scripts to decode compact tags and expand to human names using the mapping file
Anna K: I'll open the PR and include a shortbench comparing trace overhead (current vs compact vs sampled). I'll paste the results here once done. :thumbsup:
